name: Visual Foundations
description: Optional accessible static diagrams and trace prompts for all 37 current lessons.

assets.alt_text: Eight binary bits grouped together make one byte; the example shows eight positions and a bracket labelled one byte.
assets.caption: Eight bits make one byte.
assets.text_equivalent: A byte is a group of eight bits. Each bit has one of two distinguishable states, and the group can represent a larger set of values.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: A byte is a group of eight bits. Each bit has one of two distinguishable states, and the group can represent a larger set of values.
steps: Count the positions in a byte.
Explain why a pattern needs an agreed interpretation.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: A file sits inside a folder, the folder is kept on storage, and a separate copy is labelled backup.
assets.caption: Organize, store, and copy.
assets.text_equivalent: A file can be organized in a folder, stored on a device or service, and copied separately as a backup for recovery.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: A file can be organized in a folder, stored on a device or service, and copied separately as a backup for recovery.
steps: Place a fictional file inside a folder.
Describe why a separate backup helps recovery.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: A page outline contains a header, navigation, main content, and footer; meaningful landmarks help people and assistive technology move around the page.
assets.caption: Meaningful page landmarks.
assets.text_equivalent: A semantic page can expose header, navigation, main, and footer landmarks so people and assistive technology can understand and move through its structure.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: A semantic page can expose header, navigation, main, and footer landmarks so people and assistive technology can understand and move through its structure.
steps: Label header, navigation, main, and footer.
Explain why meaning should not depend on color alone.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: A simple flow shows an app asking, the learner reviewing, a narrow permission scope, and the resulting data boundary.
assets.caption: Permission choices are deliberate boundaries.
assets.text_equivalent: Follow the four boxes from the request to the data boundary. Name one question a learner should ask before allowing a permission.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Follow the four boxes from the request to the data boundary. Name one question a learner should ask before allowing a permission.
steps: Identify the data or capability it would expose.
Choose the narrowest reasonable decision in the fictional example.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: The address is separated into scheme, host, path, and query parts; each part has a different role.
assets.caption: A URL has recognizable parts.
assets.text_equivalent: Label each URL part and explain which part identifies the host versus the requested path.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Label each URL part and explain which part identifies the host versus the requested path.
steps: Describe what the path and query ask for.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: A safe response flow pauses, verifies the source through a trusted route, and chooses a safe action rather than following a pressured link.
assets.caption: Pause before responding to an unexpected message.
assets.text_equivalent: Use the flow to classify a fictional message as pause, verify, or safely ignore.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Use the flow to classify a fictional message as pause, verify, or safely ignore.
steps: Do not use the message link.
Check the sender and request using a trusted route.
Record the safe choice and why urgency is not proof.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: The comparison maps low-level and high-level choices against hardware fit and human clarity; neither side is universally best.
assets.caption: Programming languages balance machine constraints and human clarity.
assets.text_equivalent: Place a fictional task on the comparison and justify the trade-off without ranking one language as always superior.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Place a fictional task on the comparison and justify the trade-off without ranking one language as always superior.
steps: Choose the side that helps explain it.
State one cost of that choice.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: The pipeline separates source text, translation or interpretation, a running process, and observable output; a failure can occur at each stage.
assets.caption: A program moves through source, translation, processing, and output stages.
assets.text_equivalent: Identify the stage for each fictional failure message.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Identify the stage for each fictional failure message.
steps: Match it to source, translation, process, or output.

assets.alt_text: A browser sends a request, receives a response, and may store a safe local copy for later reuse without changing learner data.

assets.alt_text: The pipeline shows a goal becoming precise steps, a trace of those steps, and an observable result.
assets.caption: An algorithm turns a goal into checkable steps.
assets.text_equivalent: Rewrite a vague fictional task as a short sequence of ordered, checkable steps.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Rewrite a vague fictional task as a short sequence of ordered, checkable steps.

assets.alt_text: The small expression tree groups multiplication before addition, producing 11 rather than treating all operators as a left-to-right list.
assets.caption: Expression grouping affects the result.
assets.text_equivalent: Draw or describe the grouping for a new expression and predict its value.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Draw or describe the grouping for a new expression and predict its value.
steps: Identify the operator with higher precedence.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: An input value is bound to a variable name, transformed by a step, and sent to output; the name is a reference to a current value.
assets.caption: Values flow through names and transformations.
assets.text_equivalent: Trace a fictional input through the name, transformation, and output boxes.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Trace a fictional input through the name, transformation, and output boxes.
steps: Record the value after the transformation.
Compare the final output with the stored value.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: A condition evaluates to true or false, and the selected branch determines the result while the other branch is skipped.
assets.caption: A Boolean condition selects one of two paths.
assets.text_equivalent: Use two fictional inputs to trace both branches and state the final result.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Use two fictional inputs to trace both branches and state the final result.
steps: Record the result and the reason.

assets.alt_text: The loop cycle checks a condition, runs the body, updates state, and either repeats or exits.
assets.caption: A loop repeats by checking, acting, and updating state.
assets.text_equivalent: Fill one row of a loop trace for each cycle and identify the exit check.
assets.author: AetherLearn contributors
assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Fill one row of a loop trace for each cycle and identify the exit check.
steps: Record the state before the check.
Record the update and the next check.
practical.success_criteria: The learner can explain the labeled relationship using the fictional example without relying on color.

assets.alt_text: A caller passes inputs into a function scope, local names exist there, and a returned value crosses back to the caller.
assets.caption: Function calls create a focused scope and return a value.
assets.text_equivalent: Classify each name in a fictional call as caller state or function-local state.

assets.reduced_motion_alternative: Use the nearby text equivalent; the diagram has no animation.

practical.prompt: Use the diagram to practice: Classify each name in a fictional call as caller state or function-local state.

assets.alt_text: A collection is inspected, matching items are selected, and a transformation produces a new result without hiding the original input.

assets.alt_text: The side-by-side view shows a stack using last-in-first-out behavior and a queue using first-in-first-out behavior.

assets.alt_text: The process starts with unsorted values, compares items, then either narrows the search region or swaps values toward an ordered result.

assets.alt_text: The conceptual chart compares logarithmic, linear, and quadratic growth; it is an intuition aid, not a measured benchmark.

assets.alt_text: A rooted tree shows parent-child paths, while graph vocabulary focuses on nodes and edges without requiring a single root.
